# Client GameTest weights for -PclientShard=i/n (gradle/gametest.gradle.kts): `<simple class name> <seconds>`.
# Generated by tools/client_weights.py, never by hand. Seconds: the mean over CI runs 46126845013 (b3a2ae36) and 46127058433 (dae66414) and 46133236784 (311348f3) and 46136109973 (e67dd7b9) and 46145313302 (f29cc75b) and 46155155844 (6a7ea78f) and 46155348518 (7d2b7a9d) and 46157041825 (ed008424) and 46158184612 (2e8ea421) and 46160476291 (2c7c5de0) and 46161513043 (bf361b57) of the gap between a class's START line and the next one in each shard's client job log, the last class of a shard running to the job's final `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` line. Each run's times are scaled so its total over the classes every run ran equals the mean total (runner speed varied about 1.3x). Rounded, at least 1, the least the file accepts: a class at 1 starts and ends within a second.
# A name is simple, or fully qualified when two classes share a simple name (the full name wins). A class not listed counts as 10 s, and a name ending in Scenario as 1 s, so a new class needs no entry here and the shards still cover every
# class; an entry for a class that no longer exists is ignored. Stale numbers only unbalance the shards, never
# drop a test. Refresh from green client job logs when the shard wall times drift apart, with at least three runs, so one loaded runner does not skew a class.
# Estimates, not from a run (#1695): ContinuityPackClientTest (114 s measured whole) split into itself and ContinuityPackEnvelopesClientTest, so no class outweighs a shard. Measured whole: about 12 s to the world, 31 s for the two sequence cases, 8.6 s for each of the nine broken envelopes; each half also creates its world. Refresh both from the next runs.
